incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> PD-9876: high p95 GPU latency for model redwood-v1 in us-east-1. alert_rule=serving.latency.p95, threshold=1200ms, current=1860ms, node_group=d-ed-rt-1
pd-bot: Incident PD-9876 triggered and routed to oncall: alex (primary). Escalation policy: eng-oncall-rotation.
alex: ack'd the PD page. I'm looking. ping if others see user impact.
maya: I see a small uptick on the dashboard but no error budget breaches. 95th is spiking on a handful of replicas.
sam: grabbing runtime logs from the affected pods now.
alex: good — can someone check KV cache hit rates? if prefix caching missed it could explain the p95.
lucas: metrics snapshot — cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.92 to 0.54 between 12:03:10 and 12:05:40 UTC. concurrent_sequences also increased ~1.8x.
sam: tailing logs: ```
[2026-03-14T12:04:22Z] WARN kv_cache: miss for key user_prompt_abc
[2026-03-14T12:04:23Z] INFO scheduler: created additional batch for req 0x7f8
[2026-03-14T12:04:25Z] ERROR runtime: slow_attention_kernel: 1.9s
```
alex: looks like a burst of cold-prefixes caused extra KV loads + longer kernel paths. Could be transient client behavior. No 5xx spikes on the public API.
maya: Customer-facing latency SLO (api/generation) currently within limit on 99th. So far looks like limited impact.
pd-bot: Reminder — if a page is acknowledged but resolved automatically, we should still note if it persisted > 5m or affected customer traffic. Auto-resolve window = 3 minutes.
alex: I'm going to silence PD for 15 minutes for this alert class to avoid noise while we confirm. silencing now.
pd-bot: Silence applied to PD rule serv.latency.p95 for 15m by alex.
incident-bot: Detected auto-resolution: alert returned below threshold at 12:06:30 UTC. alert duration ~3m 20s; transient spike.
alex: marking as auto-resolved. No ongoing errors, no retries flooding.
sam: no obvious regressions in recent deploys — last deploy was 3h ago and early canaries were fine.
lucas: I think this is a noisy-sources case: a batch of internal experiments hit the endpoint, sending long sequences with low prefix overlap. Suggest we add a suppression rule for back-to-back short flares from the same node group.
maya: agree. Short term: add runbook note and lower PD sensitivity for p95 for this model during ramp windows. Long term: consider adaptive batching thresholds.
alex: action items: 1) add runbook note + link to these logs (assigned alice-docs), 2) create an automated rule to suppress duplicate alerts originating from same node_group within 2m (assigned lucas), 3) follow-up postmortem if it repeats in 24h (owner: maya).
sam: i'll paste the kubectl snippet I used for quick triage so oncall folks have it: ```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=redwood-serving --since=10m | grep "slow_attention_kernel" -A3 -B2
```
alex: thanks. labeling PD incident as "auto-resolved/no-impact" and closing the page. If it flaps again I'll escalate to oncall-2.
pd-bot: PD-9876 status: acknowledged -> resolved (auto-resolve).
incident-bot: Note: this thread recorded a transient noisy spike; recommend tuning suppression threshold from 2 alerts/min to 1 alert/min for serv.latency.p95 in us-east-1 for redwood-v1.
maya: also recording customer impact: none observed in error budgets or support tickets.
lucas: creating a quick alert-runbook PR now.
alex: thanks team. I'll follow up in the ops-queue if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
